A little about me

Experience with complex systems. A vision for smaller businesses.

I’m Saswat Prusty, an analytics and operations professional whose background spans software engineering, business analysis, SaaS product delivery, and operational planning.

At Amazon, I work on forecasting, data pipelines, and reporting that support operational planning. Earlier, I worked with hospitality software teams on financial reporting, integrations, and product delivery. I hold an MS in Business Analytics from UT Dallas and a BS in Computer Science from Manipal Institute of Technology.

I’m building this practice to help small and medium-sized businesses connect their tools, reduce repetitive work, and make clearer decisions from their data. I believe AI can be a democratizing technology: used well, it can give smaller teams access to capabilities once available mainly to much larger organizations. My goal is to make that opportunity practical, so smaller businesses can compete more effectively without taking on a giant technology program.

Outside work, I enjoy running, hiking, playing chess, and training for HYROX.

No assumed software stack and no one-size-fits-all platform. We’ll start with your tools, your constraints, and the problem you want to solve.

Frequently asked

Good questions to start with.

Do I need to replace my current software?

Usually, no. The first step is to understand what you already use and whether those tools can share the information you need. Any change should have a clear reason.

Is this only for businesses with a data team?

No. The work is designed for owners and teams who need clearer reporting or less manual work. We can start with spreadsheets and the tools you already have.

Will you use AI in every project?

No. AI is one option, not a default. If a simpler report, integration, or rule-based automation solves the problem better, that’s the right place to start.

How much does an engagement cost?

My hourly rate is $53. Before work starts, we’ll agree on the scope and estimated hours. Any third-party software or subscription costs are separate.

What happens on a discovery call?

We’ll discuss how you work today, what feels harder than it should, and whether there’s a practical first step. No preparation is required.
